condition: compressible tortuous veins above the left testis over 6 months with heaviness and dull aching after standing in a young man
level_rationale: Six months of soft tangled veins above the left testicle accompanied by testicular heaviness and a dull ache after standing in a 26-year-old man is a classic presentation of a symptomatic clinical left varicocele warranting urology specialist evaluation with scrotal Doppler ultrasonography and consideration of microsurgical repair, whereas that left testicle suddenly pulling up high with agonizing pain represents an acute surgical scrotal emergency requiring immediate emergency department detorsion evaluation.

design_note: Uses three strictly atomic reference facts centered on the symptomatic left scrotal venous swelling and standing ache (without couple subfertility to stay completely distinct from r11-084) and without naming varicocele or torsion, with a 1-word span difference (20 vs 19 words), zero stated negatives, and identical digit multisets across all 6 variants. Under reviewer_notes Rules A and D and Trend 2, escalating only f3 in a separate finite clause to sudden high-riding agonizing pain in that testicle shifts care cleanly from urology specialist evaluation (level 3) to emergency surgical evaluation (level 4).
